title: Squiffy project file
description: Makes a folder of .squiffy, .css and .js files one story. See https://squiffystory.com/project-file/

version.description: The version of the project file format. Squiffy refuses to build a project with a version it doesn't know.

id.description: Identifies the story, so a player's saved game can only be loaded into the story it came from. Any text no other story has: a new squiffy.json gets a random UUID. Keep it the same between versions of your story.

description.description: What the story is about, in a sentence or two. The published page's description, which search results and link previews show, and what sites that list stories show.
examples: A short story about a cave.

author.description: Who wrote the story. The published page's author.

cover.description: The story's cover image, by its path from the main file's folder, as the story would refer to it. The image a link to the published story shows. It's published with the story.

main.description: The story's main file, relative to this file's folder. The story starts there, and its @title is the story's title.

exclude.description: Patterns for .squiffy, .css and .js files that aren't part of the story, relative to this file's folder. * and ? match within a folder name, ** across folders, and a pattern that matches a folder leaves out everything in it.

backButton.description: Whether the published story has a Back button, which takes the player back a section or passage at a time. Set it to false to leave it out.

saveButton.description: Whether the published story has a Save button, which opens the player's list of saved games. Set it to false to leave it out.

startAnywhere.description: Whether the published story lets anyone start at any section, for a build that's for testing: "?start=section" on its address, and a Start at menu that lists the sections. It's also published with its @test sections, which are otherwise left out. A story served by the command-line tool's --serve has all this without it.

panels.description: Passages in the master section [[]] that are always to hand, such as the player's stats or inventory: beside the story, or in a dialog from a button in the header. They're rendered again as the story goes on.

passage.description: The name of a passage in the master section [[]].

label.description: The button's text, or its tooltip if it has an icon.

position.description: "side" shows the panel beside the story (or as a button, on a narrow screen). "button" shows it in a dialog from a button in the header.

icon.description: An icon for the button, in place of its label.

settings.description: Options the player can change at any time, in the Settings dialog, such as text size or content warnings. The story reads each one as settings.name, and the story's element has classes for them, such as setting-textSize-large. They're kept for the story in the player's browser, and going back, restarting and loading a saved game leave them alone.

name.description: How the story refers to the setting: settings.name.

label.description: What the Settings dialog calls it. The name if it's left out.

description.description: More about it, shown under the label.

type.description: "toggle" is on or off (true or false), "list" is one of its options, and "range" a number from min to max.

default.description: Its value until the player changes it: false for a toggle, the first option for a list, and min for a range if it's left out.

options.description: A list's options: text, or a value for the story to read and a label for the dialog.

step.description: How far apart a range's values are, e.g. 1 for whole numbers.

persistent.description: Attributes that belong to the player rather than the playthrough, such as the endings they've found. They're kept for the story in the player's browser, and restarting, going back and loading a saved game leave them as they are. {{forget}} clears them.

strings.description: The text on the published page around the story, for a story in another language. Anything left out is in English.

restartConfirm.description: Asks the player whether they're sure, when they click Restart.
restartConfirm.default: Are you sure you want to restart?

switchToDark.description: The light/dark button's tooltip, in light mode.

switchToLight.description: The light/dark button's tooltip, in dark mode.

saves.description: The Save button's tooltip, and the Saved games dialog's heading.

saveName.description: The box for a save's name.

save.description: The button that saves the game.

noSaves.description: Shown when there are no saved games.

savedGame.description: A save with no name and no text to show.

savedToday.description: When a save was made today. [time] is the time.

savedYesterday.description: When a save was made yesterday. [time] is the time.

load.description: The button that loads a save.

loadConfirm.description: Asks the player whether they're sure, when loading would lose progress. [name] is the save's name.
loadConfirm.default: Load "[name]"? You'll lose anything you've done since you last saved.

saveOptions.description: The tooltip of a save's menu button. [name] is the save's name.

overwrite.description: Replaces a save with the game as it is now.

overwriteConfirm.description: Asks the player whether they're sure, before overwriting. [name] is the save's name.

newName.description: The box for a save's new name.

saveToFile.description: Saves the game to a file.

loadFromFile.description: Loads a game from a file.

deleteConfirm.description: Asks the player whether they're sure, before deleting. [name] is the save's name.

cancel.description: Answers no to a question in the Saved games dialog.

close.description: The close button of the Saved games dialog and the panels' dialog.

wrongStory.description: Shown when a saved game is from a different story.
wrongStory.default: This saved game is for a different story.

notASave.description: Shown when a file isn't a saved game.
notASave.default: This file isn't a saved game.

cantSave.description: Shown when the game couldn't be saved in the browser.
cantSave.default: The game couldn't be saved. Try Save to file instead.

settings.description: The Settings button's tooltip, the Settings dialog's heading, and the text of {{settings}} links.

resetSettings.description: The Settings dialog's button that puts every setting back to its default.

startAt.description: The Start at button's tooltip and the Start at menu's heading, for a story with "startAnywhere".

findSection.description: The Start at menu's search box.

testSections.description: The Start at menu's heading for sections marked with @test.

allSections.description: The Start at menu's heading for the other sections.

noSection.description: Shown when the address names a section the story doesn't have. [name] is the name.

map.description: Where sections and passages have been put on the editor's story map. The editor writes this: only what's been moved by hand is here, and the map lays out the rest.

sections.description: Positions of sections, by name, as [x, y].

passages.description: Positions of passages, by their section's name and then their own, as [x, y].
